source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 3, 65. 66. Τὸ ὑπερασπισμὸν καρδίας μόχθον αὐτοῖς, ὅτι δώσεις ἀὐτοῖς μόχθον εἰς αἴσθησιν τοῦ πόσος ὑπῆρχες ὑπερασπίζων αὐτῶν, ἵνα σὲ καὶ πάλιν ζητήσωσιν. εἰ δὲ μή, καταδιώξεις αὐτοὺς ἐν ὀργῇ σου.
pass_a_gloss: The “hyperaspismos / shielding of heart” is a toil for them, because you will give them a toil unto perception of how great you were when hyperaspismos / shielding them, so that they may seek you again. And if not, you will chase them in your wrath.
pass_b_english: The “shielding of heart” (Lamentations 3:65–66) is a toil for them, because you will give them a toil unto perception of how great you were when shielding them, so that they may seek you again. And if not, you will chase them in your wrath.

choices.why: Origen allegorizes God’s word as sword at Lam 4:9.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Origen’s Greek Lamentations fragments. Sense checked against Klostermann GCS III. Modern English not copied. OET = no previous English translation.
